name: Rwanda
snapshot: A tightly controlled, fast-modernising state under Paul Kagame, put under US sanctions in 2026 for its army's role alongside the M23 rebels in Congo.
culture: Rwanda's people share one language, Kinyarwanda, and the government has erased official ethnic labels since the 1994 genocide, in which some 800,000 Tutsi and moderate Hutu were killed in 100 days. Remembrance, kwibuka, is observed each April. Umuganda, a monthly morning of compulsory community work, reflects a strongly organised society. Intore warrior dances are a national art.
society: Kigali is famously clean and orderly, and the government has invested in conference tourism, gorilla trekking and sponsorship of football clubs like Arsenal and PSG. Growth has been strong and health outcomes have improved sharply. But critics are jailed or killed abroad, and the press is tightly controlled.
situation: Paul Kagame, effectively in charge since 1994, won a fourth term in 2024 with 99 percent. UN experts say Rwandan troops fight alongside M23 in eastern Congo; Rwanda says it acts against Hutu militias tied to the genocide. A US-brokered peace deal with Congo was signed in 2025, but in early 2026 Washington sanctioned Rwanda's military and senior officials for violating it. Kagame called the sanctions insults and accused the US of bias toward Kinshasa.
power: A presidential republic dominated by the Rwandan Patriotic Front. The president is directly elected for five-year terms, and a 2015 referendum allows Kagame to stay until 2034; opposition parties operate under tight limits.

leaders.gov: Prime Minister Justin Nsengiyumva, since July 2025
